title: Air India Extends Saudi Cancellations to October 24, Offers Free Rebooking to November 10
excerpt: Air India and Air India Express will not fly to Jeddah, Riyadh or Dammam until October 24, extending Friday's October 20 halt as Houthi strikes continue; eligible passengers can rebook free, reroute via other Gulf cities, or take a full refund.
body:
• Air India and Air India Express have extended their suspension of flights to Jeddah, Riyadh and Dammam to October 24, 2026 — four days beyond the October 20 date announced on Friday.
  • Passengers with bookings issued on or before October 15 for travel between October 9 and 25 can make one complimentary date change for travel up to November 10, rebook from an alternative Gulf station, or take a full refund.
  • IndiGo had already extended its Saudi cancellations to October 24 on Thursday, and Akasa Air has suspended Riyadh flights to October 24 and Jeddah flights to October 21.
  • If you hold a Saudi booking: do not head to the airport — rebook or claim your refund through the airline's contact centre or city office, and keep your new travel on or before November 10 to use the free change.

Air India and Air India Express have extended the suspension of flights to and from Jeddah, Riyadh and Dammam in Saudi Arabia until October 24, the airlines announced on Saturday, pushing the halt four days beyond the October 20 date set only a day earlier as Houthi strikes continue in the region.

The extension is the latest step in a rolling series of cancellations that began with a suspension to October 17, was extended to October 20 on Friday, and now runs to October 24. In its advisory, reported by The Hindu BusinessLine, Air India cited the prevailing security situation in West Asia following Houthi rebel strikes.

"In view of the prevailing situation, Air India and Air India Express have temporarily suspended flights to and from Jeddah, Riyadh and Dammam until 24 October 2026."

— Air India travel advisory

Your rebooking and refund options

Guests holding confirmed Air India or Air India Express bookings issued on or before October 15, 2026, with travel dates between October 9 and October 25, are eligible for a one-time complimentary date change on their respective airline, for travel up to November 10, 2026.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=XUlS8qeN2iQ

Passengers who do not want to rebook on the original sector for a later date can instead rebook from an alternative station in the Gulf region served by their airline, subject to availability. Air India guests may rebook to or from Dubai or Doha. Air India Express guests may rebook to or from Abu Dhabi, Al Ain, Bahrain, Doha, Dubai, Kuwait, Muscat, Ras Al Khaimah, Salalah or Sharjah. Passengers choosing an alternative station must make their own arrangements to reach that departure point and meet its visa and entry requirements. Anyone whose flight was cancelled and who no longer wishes to travel can opt for a full refund.

Air India said its teams are available through its contact centres and city booking offices in Gulf stations and India to assist with rebooking and refunds, according to the advisory reproduced by Kashmir Outlook: Air India on +91 1169329333 or +91 1169329999, and Air India Express on +91 124 6935600.

Other Indian carriers have moved the same way

Air India is not acting alone. IndiGo on Thursday extended cancellations to Riyadh, Jeddah, Dammam and Madinah until October 24 inclusive, saying it was notifying affected customers on their booking contact details. Akasa Air has extended its Riyadh suspension to October 24 and its Jeddah suspension to October 21, offering a full refund credited to the original payment source within seven days or rescheduling at no additional cost, according to The Hindu BusinessLine's report on the IndiGo and Akasa extensions.

https://x.com/airindia/status/2111370834753589672

Why flights remain suspended

The disruptions follow the October 10 attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh. ANI reported the death toll from that attack has risen to 13, after the Indian Embassy in Riyadh confirmed that an Indian national who had been injured died. On Friday, Yemen's internationally recognised government accused the Houthi militia of targeting Aden International Airport with two missiles that landed near a Yemenia Airlines aircraft preparing for take-off to Cairo, according to Information Minister Moammar Al-Eryani.

For the large Indian workforce in Saudi Arabia and families travelling for work, visits and pilgrimage, the practical effect is a second weekend with no direct Air India or Air India Express service to the Kingdom's three main Indian gateways. Air India said it continues to monitor the situation closely and will keep guests informed of further updates, with supporting affected passengers and minimising inconvenience as its stated priority. Travellers with bookings after October 24 should still check their flight status before travelling, as every extension in this sequence has been announced close to the previous deadline.
